text:
Maya Chen: Hey @eng-runtime — heads up: we have the webinar + launch post scheduled for next Wednesday. Marketing needs final, validated benchmark numbers (latency p50/p95/p99, throughput, and cost per 1M tokens) to put in the deck and blog. Can the runtime team do a reproducible rerun and a quick sanity check for the models below?

Maya Chen: Models of interest: redwood-3b-gguf, redwood-7b-q4, and a 13b float16 baseline. Target seq lengths: 512 and 2048. Workloads: single-stream low-latency (concurrency=1) and bursty throughput (concurrency=16) with typical chat-ish prompts.

Maya Chen: Deliverables we need:
- run artifacts (raw logs + consolidated table)
- exact command lines / docker images + env vars used
- sample input payloads (one chat prompt set for 512 and one for 2048) and one short sample output per model
- notes about variability (random seeds, warmup, caching), and any abnormal failures seen

Sam Ortiz: Got it — we can take this. Quick Qs: do you want tokens-per-second at the model output layer or after post-processing (we usually report model-side tokens/s)? Also do you need per-token cost with current pricing or normalized ops cost?

Maya Chen: model-side tokens/s is fine. For cost please do both: our current hosted price estimate (use dev pricing table) and a normalized GPU-op estimate so we can compare across infra.

Sam Ortiz: Cool. Plan: I'll run a full pass today for 512, then do 2048 tomorrow morning. I'll push artifacts to the bench repo and ping here when done. ETA for consolidated table: EOD tomorrow.

Chris Patel: Adding the smoke commands we'll run. Copy/paste in case useful: 

```
# run single-stream
docker run --rm -e MODEL=redwood-7b-q4 ghcr.io/redwood/bench:latest \n  ./bench --model $MODEL --concurrency 1 --seq_len 512 --batch_size 1 --runs 50 --seed 42 --output /outputs/$MODEL-512.json\n
# run bursty throughput
docker run --rm -e MODEL=redwood-7b-q4 ghcr.io/redwood/bench:latest \n  ./bench --model $MODEL --concurrency 16 --seq_len 2048 --batch_size 4 --runs 20 --seed 42 --output /outputs/$MODEL-2048.json
```

Chris Patel: Note: enable KV cache warmup (--warmup_steps 5) to be consistent with prior runs. Also we pin CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and set NCCL_DEBUG=INFO for logs.

Sam Ortiz: Also calling out variability: for the 2048 runs we usually see ~10-15% jitter depending on kernel selection. We'll include median + 90/99 percentiles and raw per-request logs so you can inspect outliers.

Zoe Park: For the blog we want a 1‑sentence blurb for each model (e.g., "7B quantized: X ms p99 at seq=512, good price/latency tradeoff"). Sam — can you add one-sentence plain-English takeaways with the artifact?

Sam Ortiz: Yep. We'll add takeaways and a small CSV with columns: model, seq_len, concurrency, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, tokens_per_s, cost_per_1M_tokens_hosted, gpu_op_estimate.

Maya Chen: Great. Can you also sanity-run one very short smoke test that we can embed in the webinar demo (so the demo doesn't rely on production endpoints)? Something that returns <1200 tokens quickly.

Chris Patel: Use this minimal payload for the smoke run: 

```
{"inputs": [{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the key points of this paragraph in three bullets."}], "max_tokens": 200}
```

Chris Patel: Sample expected output format (trimmed):

"- Bullet 1
- Bullet 2
- Bullet 3"

dev-bench-bot: bench-runner started job 9812 for redwood-7b-q4 seq=512 (owner: sam.ortiz). Logs: https://bench.internal/reports/9812

Sam Ortiz: Pushed initial 512 artifacts to https://bench.internal/reports/9812 — includes raw logs, consolidated CSV, and a README with exact commands and env. I'll kick off 2048 now.

Maya Chen: Perfect, thanks. If the 2048 p99 looks bad, please flag alternatives (e.g., reduce batch size, use q4->q5 variant, or suggest dedupe/caching tweaks).

Sam Ortiz: Will do. If we see signs of kernel thrash we'll note recommended quantization/profile changes. ETA final consolidated table: tomorrow EOD.

Jack Rivera: Thanks team — very helpful. If you want comms support for interpreting results or writing the one-sentence takeaways, ping me and I can draft copy. :rocket:

Sam Ortiz: Appreciate it. I'll post again with final CSV + plain-English takeaways when 2048 finishes.

Maya Chen: Awesome — we'll hold off on the slide updates until you confirm. Thanks all!
